```{r shared-setup}
#| include: false
#| cache: false
source("scripts/analysis_setup.R")
# The cached quality-screen sensitivity analysis sources data_quality.R, so a
# change to the flag rules must invalidate the cache.
configure_analysis_cache(project_path("scripts", "data_quality.R"))

# APA-style p-values: no leading zero, "< .001" below .001.
format_p_value <- function(p) {
  ifelse(p < .001, "< .001", sub("^0", "", sprintf("%.3f", p)))
}
```

## Rating items

Each participant rated all seven visualizations on four items, each on a 5-point scale.
The comparison item was asked right after Task 1; the other three after Task 2, when
participants had used each visualization in both tasks. Comparisons within an item are
unaffected, but differences between items may partly reflect this timing.

| Item | Label on this page | Survey wording or label | Response scale | Asked |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A301 | Helpful for comparison | "Helpful for comparison" | 1 = very unhelpful … 5 = very helpful | After Task 1 |
| A302 | Helpful for detection and integration | "Helpful for detection" | 1 = very unhelpful … 5 = very helpful | After Task 2 |
| A303 | Would use in publication or presentation | "I would prefer to use this visualization for representing signal mean and standard error in a publication or presentation" (survey label "Usage material") | 1 = very unlikely … 5 = very likely | After Task 2 |
| A304 | Aesthetically appealing | "Appealing" | 1 = very unappealing … 5 = very appealing | After Task 2 |

: Rating items. A303 measures the likelihood of using a visualization, not its helpfulness. A301 was answered right after the comparison task, before participants had seen Task 2. {.striped}

::: {.callout-note title="Limitation: fixed item order"}
Within every rating question the visualizations were listed in the same order for every
participant: Adjacent plots first and Basic topoplot always last. Order and context effects
therefore cannot be separated from differences between visualizations.
:::

## Rating data preparation and descriptive summary

```{r}

question_labels <- c(
  A301 = "Helpful for comparison",
  A302 = "Helpful for detection and integration",
  A303 = "Would use in publication or presentation",
  A304 = "Aesthetically appealing"
)

# All four questions presented the visualization types in the same order.
# The A304 columns retain that order in the export, but their suffixes are
# nonsequential (01, 06, 02, 03, 04, 05, 07).
rating_columns <- list(
  A301 = sprintf("A301_%02d", seq_along(vistypes)),
  A302 = sprintf("A302_%02d", seq_along(vistypes)),
  A303 = sprintf("A303_%02d", seq_along(vistypes)),
  A304 = c(
    "A304_01", "A304_06", "A304_02", "A304_03",
    "A304_04", "A304_05", "A304_07"
  )
)

rating_key <- purrr::imap_dfr(
  rating_columns,
  \(columns, question_code) tibble(
    question_code = question_code,
    rating_column = columns,
    vistype = vistypes
  )
)
```

```{r subjective-rating-validation}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Validation checks"
#| results: hide

if (!identical(names(rating_columns), names(question_labels)) ||
    any(lengths(rating_columns) != length(vistypes)) ||
    anyDuplicated(rating_key$rating_column) ||
    nrow(rating_key) != 28L) {
  stop("The subjective-rating key must contain 28 unique survey columns.")
}

# Validate the explicit key against the question labels embedded in the first
# row of the LimeSurvey export. Stop rather than silently relabel results if the
# questionnaire changes in a future export.
rating_key_validation <- rating_key %>%
  mutate(
    survey_label = as.character(
      unlist(legend[1, rating_column], use.names = FALSE)
    ),
    label_matches = stringr::str_detect(
      survey_label,
      stringr::fixed(vistype)
    )
  )

if (any(is.na(rating_key_validation$survey_label)) ||
    any(!rating_key_validation$label_matches)) {
  stop("The subjective-rating key does not match the embedded survey labels.")
}
```

```{r}
likert <- data %>%
  select(ID, all_of(rating_key$rating_column)) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    -ID,
    names_to = "rating_column",
    values_to = "rating_raw"
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    rating_key %>% select(rating_column, question_code, vistype),
    by = "rating_column"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    vistype = factor(
      vistype,
      levels = vistypes
    ),

    question = factor(
      question_code,
      levels = names(question_labels),
      labels = unname(question_labels)
    ),

    rating = as.integer(
      stringr::str_extract(as.character(rating_raw), "^-?\\d+")
    ),

    rating = if_else(
      rating %in% 1:5,
      rating,
      NA_integer_
    )
  ) %>%
  select(ID, question, vistype, rating)
```

```{r likert-summary-table}
likert_table <- likert %>%
  group_by(vistype, question) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_rating = round(mean(rating, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    names_from = question,
    values_from = mean_rating
  ) %>%
  # Basic topoplot first (the reference), then the survey order. No composite
  # score: the four items measure different things (A303 is likelihood of use)
  # and A301 was asked at a different time, so an equal-weight sum has no
  # clear meaning (audit U10).
  arrange(vistype != "basic", vistype)

likert_table |>
  mutate(vistype = table_vistype(vistype)) |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    digits = 2,
    col.names = c("Visualization type", unname(question_labels)),
    caption = "Mean subjective ratings by visualization type (raw means, 1–5)",
    table.attr = kable_table_attributes
  )
```
## Ordinal mixed-effects models

```{r}
likert_model_data <- likert |>
  filter(!is.na(rating)) |>
  mutate(
    ID = factor(ID),
    vistype = droplevels(factor(vistype)),
    rating_ord = ordered(rating, levels = 1:5)
  )

likert_models <- likert_model_data |>
  (\(data) split(data, data$question))() |>
  map(
    \(data_question) clmm(
      rating_ord ~ vistype + (1 | ID),
      data = data_question,
      Hess = TRUE
    )
  )

likert_estimates <- imap_dfr(
  likert_models,
  function(model, question_name) {

    emmeans(
      model,
      ~ vistype,
      mode = "mean.class"
    ) |>
      confint() |>
      as.data.frame() |>
      transmute(
        question = question_name,
        vistype,
        estimated_rating = mean.class,
        lower_ci = asymp.LCL,
        upper_ci = asymp.UCL
      )
  }
)

likert_estimates |>
  mutate(vistype = table_vistype(vistype)) |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    digits = 2,
    col.names = c(
      "Evaluation criterion",
      "Visualization type",
      "Expected rating, typical participant",
      "Lower 95% CI",
      "Upper 95% CI"
    ),
    caption = "Expected ratings for a typical participant (participant effect at zero)",
    table.attr = kable_table_attributes
  )

model_table_note(paste0(
  "Separate cumulative-link mixed models with logit link are fitted for each ",
  "evaluation criterion: <code>rating_ord ~ vistype + (1 | ID)</code>. ",
  "Estimated marginal means use <code>mode = &quot;mean.class&quot;</code>: they are ",
  "expected ratings on the 1–5 scale for a typical participant (participant effect ",
  "set to zero), not averages over all participants, with asymptotic pointwise 95% ",
  "confidence intervals (not adjusted for multiplicity). They stay close to the raw ",
  "means (see the model checks below)."
))
```

### Model checks and sensitivity analyses

```{r likert-model-checks}
#| cache: false
# 1. Proportional odds: cumulative-link mixed models with a participant random
#    intercept, with and without visualization-specific thresholds (nominal
#    effects), compared by likelihood-ratio test. clmm2 is used because clmm does
#    not support nominal effects (it ignores the argument with a warning); a
#    fixed-effects clm test would treat each participant's 7 ratings as
#    independent and give too-small p values.
po_tests <- likert_model_data |>
  (\(data) split(data, data$question))() |>
  imap_dfr(function(data_question, question_name) {
    po_fit <- clmm2(
      location = rating_ord ~ vistype, random = ID,
      data = data_question, Hess = TRUE
    )
    npo_fit <- clmm2(
      location = rating_ord ~ 1, nominal = ~ vistype, random = ID,
      data = data_question, Hess = TRUE
    )
    lr_statistic <- 2 * (npo_fit$logLik - po_fit$logLik)
    df <- npo_fit$edf - po_fit$edf
    tibble(
      question = question_name,
      lr_statistic = lr_statistic,
      df = df,
      p_value = pchisq(lr_statistic, df, lower.tail = FALSE)
    )
  })

# 2. Expected ratings (typical participant) vs raw means.
raw_vs_model <- likert |>
  group_by(question, vistype) |>
  summarise(raw_mean = mean(rating, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(question = as.character(question), vistype = as.character(vistype)) |>
  inner_join(
    likert_estimates |> mutate(vistype = as.character(vistype)),
    by = c("question", "vistype")
  ) |>
  mutate(abs_difference = abs(estimated_rating - raw_mean))
max_raw_model_difference <- max(raw_vs_model$abs_difference)

# 3. Linear mixed model on the 1–5 ratings: same Dunnett contrasts vs Basic.
likert_lmm_contrasts <- likert_model_data |>
  (\(data) split(data, data$question))() |>
  imap_dfr(function(data_question, question_name) {
    fit <- lmer(rating ~ vistype + (1 | ID), data = data_question)
    question_emmeans <- emmeans(fit, ~ vistype)
    set.seed(20261118)  # adjust = "mvt" integrates numerically (Monte Carlo)
    contrast(
      question_emmeans,
      method = "trt.vs.ctrl",
      ref = which(question_emmeans@levels$vistype == "basic"),
      adjust = "mvt"
    ) |>
      confint() |>
      as.data.frame() |>
      transmute(
        question = question_name,
        vistype = stringr::str_remove(contrast, " - basic$"),
        lmm_difference = estimate,
        lmm_lower = lower.CL,
        lmm_upper = upper.CL
      )
  })

po_tests |>
  mutate(p_value = format_p_value(p_value)) |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    digits = 1,
    col.names = c("Evaluation criterion", "LR statistic", "df", "p"),
    caption = paste(
      "Proportional-odds check: cumulative-link mixed model (participant random",
      "intercept) vs the same model with visualization-specific thresholds",
      "(likelihood-ratio test)"
    ),
    table.attr = kable_table_attributes
  )
```

**Proportional odds.** The likelihood-ratio test rejects proportional odds for
`r sum(po_tests$p_value < .05)` of 4 criteria (p from
`r format_p_value(min(po_tests$p_value))` to `r format_p_value(max(po_tests$p_value))`):
the visualizations differ in how ratings are spread over the scale, not only in their
location. The analysis therefore reports expected (mean) ratings for a typical participant,
which stay close to the raw means (largest absolute difference `r sprintf("%.2f", max_raw_model_difference)`
scale points), rather than interpreting the odds ratios.

::: {.callout-note title="Seeing the proportional-odds problem — Expand" collapse="true"}

**What the figure shows.** Each small panel is one visualization (columns) on one rating
question (rows). It compares that visualization with Basic topoplot at four cut-offs of
the 1–5 scale: rated at least 2, at least 3, at least 4, and rated 5.

**How to read one point.** Its height is the odds ratio against Basic: how much more
(or less) likely people were to rate the visualization at least this high.

- **1** (blue dashed line): the same as Basic.
- **4**: four times Basic's odds; **1/4**: a quarter of Basic's odds.
- The axis is logarithmic, so "4 times" and "a quarter" are equally far from the line.

**How to read the line.**

- **Flat:** the visualization moves all ratings up or down evenly. One number (an odds
  ratio) would describe it well. This is what the ordinal model assumes ("proportional
  odds").
- **Rising** (low on the left, higher on the right): many people gave it a low rating,
  but some still gave it a high one. Opinions are divided.
- **Falling:** almost nobody gave it a low rating, but its lead over Basic shrinks
  among the top ratings.

**What it means here.** Several lines are clearly not flat. For example, Bivariate
corner and Bivariate range rise steeply for comparison and for appeal: many participants
rated them low, yet some still rated them 4 or 5. A single odds ratio would hide this,
which is why this page reports mean ratings instead.

```{r likert-po-figure}
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 8
#| fig-alt: "Grid of small line charts, one per visualization and rating question. Each shows the odds ratio against Basic topoplot at the cut-offs rated at least 2, 3, 4 and 5. Several lines slope steeply, especially for Bivariate corner and Bivariate range on comparison and appeal."
# Odds ratio against Basic at each cut-off, computed from the raw rating shares
# (not from the model); 0.5 is added to counts so that empty cells stay finite.
likert_po_steps <- purrr::map_dfr(2:5, \(cutoff) {
  likert |>
    filter(!is.na(rating)) |>
    group_by(question, vistype) |>
    summarise(share = (sum(rating >= cutoff) + 0.5) / (n() + 1), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(cutoff = cutoff)
}) |>
  group_by(question, cutoff) |>
  mutate(odds_ratio = exp(qlogis(share) - qlogis(share[vistype == "basic"]))) |>
  ungroup() |>
  filter(vistype != "basic") |>
  mutate(
    vistype = droplevels(vistype),
    vis_label = factor(table_vistype(vistype), levels = table_vistype(levels(vistype)))
  )

ggplot(likert_po_steps, aes(cutoff, odds_ratio, group = vis_label)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", colour = basic_accent) +
  geom_line(colour = "grey45", linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_point(size = 2.4, colour = "#222222") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2:5) +
  scale_y_log10(breaks = 4^(-2:3), labels = c("1/16", "1/4", "1", "4", "16", "64")) +
  facet_grid(
    question ~ vis_label,
    labeller = labeller(question = label_wrap_gen(22), vis_label = label_wrap_gen(12))
  ) +
  labs(x = "Rated at least", y = "Odds ratio vs Basic topoplot (log scale)") +
  # Sizes balanced at the ~1100 px display width like the other rating figures
  # (16 in there, 13 in here, so their sizes x 13/16): panel labels near the
  # visualization labels, tick numbers near the tick numbers there.
  plot_theme(base_size = 26) +
  theme(
    axis.text = element_text(size = 23),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 26),
    strip.background = element_blank(),
    strip.text = element_text(size = 26),
    strip.text.x = element_text(lineheight = 0.45),
    strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0, lineheight = 0.45),
    panel.border = element_rect(fill = NA, colour = "grey85")
  )
```

Computed from the raw rating shares, not from the model; 0.5 is added to each count so
that a cut-off nobody reached still gives a finite value.

:::

**Random-effects structure.** Each participant gave exactly one rating per visualization and
criterion. Participant-specific visualization effects (`(1 + vistype | ID)`) would have one
observation per random effect and are not identifiable separately from the observation-level
latent error, so the random intercept is the maximal identifiable structure. The linear mixed
model below is a sensitivity check that does not rely on proportional odds.

## Model-estimated ratings

```{r}
#| cache: false
#| fig-width: 16
#| fig-height: 11
question_columns <- unname(question_labels)

likert_vistype_order <- c(
  "basic",
  "adjacent",
  "triple_CI",
  "uncert_markers",
  "animation",
  "bivariate_range",
  "bivariate_corner"
)

likert_display_labels <- setNames(
  figure_vistype(likert_vistype_order),
  likert_vistype_order
)

likert_panel_titles <- c(
  "Helpful for comparison" = "Helpful for comparison",
  "Helpful for detection and integration" = "Helpful for detection & integration",
  "Would use in publication or presentation" = "Would use in publication",
  "Aesthetically appealing" = "Aesthetically appealing"
)

# Verbal anchors of 1 and 5 on each item's response scale (see "Rating items"),
# shown under the rating axis of the estimate figure (audit V2).
likert_anchors <- list(
  "Helpful for comparison" = c("very unhelpful", "very helpful"),
  "Helpful for detection and integration" = c("very unhelpful", "very helpful"),
  "Would use in publication or presentation" = c("very unlikely", "very likely"),
  "Aesthetically appealing" = c("very unappealing", "very appealing")
)

# Sizes of the Likert figures: site version (nominal sizes, drawn at 96/180 of
# nominal by showtext) or print version (true pt; audit V7). Label and point
# sizes in mm as ggplot2 expects.
likert_figure_sizes <- function(print = FALSE) {
  if (print) {
    list(base = print_text$text, title = print_text$text, axis_x = print_text$small,
         labels = print_text$text / ggplot2::.pt, values = print_text$small / ggplot2::.pt,
         caption = print_text$text, point = 1.5, line = 0.4, margin = 4,
         label_space = 84, anchor = print_text$small / ggplot2::.pt, anchor_row = 10)
  } else {
    # Balanced at the ~1100 px display width of the 16-in site figure (audit
    # V2): panel titles one step above the visualization labels, tick numbers
    # and anchors close to the value labels. anchor_row is the height (pt) of
    # the anchor line under each panel.
    list(base = 20, title = 36, axis_x = 28, labels = 34 / ggplot2::.pt,
         values = 30 / ggplot2::.pt, caption = 30, point = 3, line = 0.55,
         margin = 12, label_space = 215, anchor = 26 / ggplot2::.pt, anchor_row = 22)
  }
}

make_likert_estimate_plot <- function(
  question_name,
  show_x = TRUE,
  show_labels = TRUE,
  print = FALSE
) {
  s <- likert_figure_sizes(print)

  plot_data <- likert_estimates |>
    filter(question == question_name) |>
    mutate(
      colour_group = if_else(vistype == "basic", "basic", "other"),
    
      display_label = unname(
        likert_display_labels[as.character(vistype)]
      ),
    
      vistype = factor(
        vistype,
        levels = rev(likert_vistype_order)
      )
    )

  p <- ggplot(
    plot_data,
      aes(
    x = estimated_rating,
    y = vistype,
    colour = colour_group
  )
  ) +
    geom_errorbar(
      aes(
        xmin = lower_ci,
        xmax = upper_ci
      ),
      orientation = "y",
      width = 0.12,
      linewidth = s$line
    ) +
    geom_point(size = s$point) +

    # Estimated values
    geom_text(
      aes(label = sprintf("%.1f", estimated_rating)),
      nudge_y = 0.32,
      vjust = 0.5,
      size = s$values
    ) +

    scale_colour_manual(
  values = c(
    basic = basic_accent,
    other = "#222222"
  ),
  guide = "none"
) +

    scale_x_continuous(
      breaks = 1:5,
      labels = function(x) sprintf("%.0f", x),
      expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.02))
    ) +

    # Hide ordinary y-axis labels
    scale_y_discrete(
      labels = NULL,
      expand = expansion(add = 0.5)
    ) +

    # Show custom labels placed slightly outside the panel
    coord_cartesian(
      xlim = c(1, 5),
      clip = "off"
    ) +

    labs(
      title = unname(likert_panel_titles[question_name]),
      x = NULL,
      y = NULL
    ) +

    plot_theme(base_size = s$base) +

    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(
        hjust = 0.5,
        face = "bold",
        size = s$title
      ),
      axis.text.x = element_text(size = s$axis_x),
      axis.title.x = element_text(size = s$axis_x),
      axis.text.y = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
      axis.line.y = element_blank(),
      panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
      plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),

      # Space for custom labels
       plot.margin = margin(
    t = 5.5,
    r = 5.5,
        # Small: the anchor line follows directly under the axis.
        b = if (print) 1 else 3,
    l = if (show_labels) s$label_space else s$margin
  )
    )

  if (show_labels) {
    p <- p +
      geom_text(
        data = plot_data,
        aes(
          x = 0.9,
          y = vistype,
          label = display_label,
          colour = colour_group
        ),
        inherit.aes = FALSE,
        hjust = 1,
        size = s$labels,
        lineheight = 1
      )
  }

  if (!show_x) {
    p <- p +
      theme(
        axis.title.x = element_blank(),
        axis.text.x = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks.x = element_blank()
      )
  }

  p
}

# Anchor line under a panel: the verbal labels of 1 and 5, aligned with the ends
# of the rating axis (same x range as the panel above it: 1 to 5 plus the 2%
# expansion). Stacked under its panel in the patchwork grid, which aligns the
# two panels.
make_likert_anchor_row <- function(question_name, print = FALSE) {
  s <- likert_figure_sizes(print)
  anchors <- likert_anchors[[question_name]]
  x_range <- c(1, 5) + c(-1, 1) * 0.02 * 4
  ggplot() +
    annotate(
      "text", x = x_range[1], y = 1, label = anchors[1], hjust = 0, vjust = 1,
      size = s$anchor, family = "Lato", colour = "grey30"
    ) +
    annotate(
      "text", x = x_range[2], y = 1, label = anchors[2], hjust = 1, vjust = 1,
      size = s$anchor, family = "Lato", colour = "grey30"
    ) +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = x_range, ylim = c(0, 1), expand = FALSE, clip = "off") +
    theme_void() +
    theme(plot.margin = margin(0, 5.5, 0, 0))
}

# Site version, or with print = TRUE the print version (audit V7). Every panel
# shows the 1-5 axis with its item's anchors underneath (audit V2).
make_likert_estimate_figure <- function(print = FALSE) {
  s <- likert_figure_sizes(print)
  p1 <- make_likert_estimate_plot(question_columns[1], show_x = TRUE, print = print)
  p2 <- make_likert_estimate_plot(
    question_columns[2], show_x = TRUE, show_labels = FALSE, print = print
  )
  p3 <- make_likert_estimate_plot(question_columns[3], show_x = TRUE, print = print)
  p4 <- make_likert_estimate_plot(
    question_columns[4], show_x = TRUE, show_labels = FALSE, print = print
  )
  anchor_rows <- purrr::map(question_columns, make_likert_anchor_row, print = print)

  wrap_plots(
    p1, p2, anchor_rows[[1]], anchor_rows[[2]],
    p3, p4, anchor_rows[[3]], anchor_rows[[4]],
    ncol = 2,
    heights = grid::unit(
      c(1, s$anchor_row, 1, s$anchor_row),
      c("null", "pt", "null", "pt")
    )
  ) +
    plot_annotation(
      caption = "Expected rating, typical participant (pointwise 95% CI)",
      theme = theme(
        plot.caption = element_text(
          hjust = 0.5,
          size = s$caption,
          family = "Lato",
          lineheight = 1.1,
          margin = if (print) margin(t = 4, b = 2) else margin(t = 10, b = 6)
        ),
        plot.caption.position = "plot",
        plot.margin = if (print) margin(3, 4, 4, 4) else margin(6, 12, 12, 12)
      )
    )
}

likert_estimate_figure <- make_likert_estimate_figure()

likert_estimate_figure

ggsave_st(
  project_path("figures", "likert_estimate_figure.png"),
  likert_estimate_figure,
  width = 16,
  height = 11,
  units = "in",
  dpi = 180,
  device = ragg::agg_png,
```

## Differences relative to Basic topoplot

```{r likert-basic-contrasts}
#| include: false

likert_contrasts <- imap_dfr(
  likert_models,
  function(model, question_name) {
    question_emmeans <- emmeans(
      model,
      ~ vistype,
      mode = "mean.class"
    )

    basic_reference <- which(
      question_emmeans@levels$vistype == "basic"
    )

    set.seed(20261118)  # adjust = "mvt" integrates numerically (Monte Carlo)
    contrast_result <- contrast(
      question_emmeans,
      method = "trt.vs.ctrl",
      adjust = "mvt",
      ref = basic_reference
    ) |>
      confint() |>
      as.data.frame()

    lower_column <- grep(
      "lower.CL$|asymp.LCL$",
      names(contrast_result),
      value = TRUE
    )[1]
    upper_column <- grep(
      "upper.CL$|asymp.UCL$",
      names(contrast_result),
      value = TRUE
    )[1]

    contrast_result |>
      transmute(
        question = question_name,
        vistype = stringr::str_remove(contrast, " - basic$"),
        difference = estimate,
        lower_ci = .data[[lower_column]],
        upper_ci = .data[[upper_column]]
      )
  }
) |>
  group_by(question) |>
  mutate(
    vistype = factor(vistype, levels = rev(likert_vistype_order[-1])),
    # Highlight contrasts whose Dunnett-adjusted interval excludes zero (no
    # "leader": differences between non-reference visualizations are not tested).
    excludes_zero = lower_ci > 0 | upper_ci < 0
  ) |>
  ungroup()

likert_contrast_limit <- max(
  2,
  ceiling(
    max(abs(c(likert_contrasts$lower_ci, likert_contrasts$upper_ci)), na.rm = TRUE) * 10
  ) / 10
)

format_rating_difference <- function(x) {
  ifelse(
    abs(x) < 0.05,
    "0.0",
    sprintf("%+.1f", x)
  )
}

make_likert_contrast_plot <- function(
  question_name,
  show_x = TRUE,
  show_labels = TRUE,
  print = FALSE
) {
  s <- likert_figure_sizes(print)
  plot_data <- likert_contrasts |>
    filter(question == question_name)

  p <- ggplot(
    plot_data,
    aes(x = difference, y = vistype)
  ) +
    geom_vline(
      xintercept = 0,
      linetype = "dashed",
      linewidth = if (print) s$line else 0.6,
      colour = basic_accent
    ) +
    geom_errorbar(
      aes(xmin = lower_ci, xmax = upper_ci, colour = excludes_zero),
      orientation = "y",
      width = 0.12,
      linewidth = s$line
    ) +
    geom_point(aes(colour = excludes_zero), size = s$point) +
    geom_text(
      aes(
        label = format_rating_difference(difference),
        colour = excludes_zero
      ),
      nudge_y = 0.3,
      vjust = 0.5,
      size = s$values
    ) +
    scale_colour_manual(
      values = c(`FALSE` = "#222222", `TRUE` = "#D94B5B"),
      guide = "none"
    ) +
    scale_y_discrete(
      labels = function(x) unname(likert_display_labels[x]),
      expand = expansion(add = 0.5)
    ) +
    scale_x_continuous(
      breaks = -2:2,
      labels = function(x) format_rating_difference(x),
      expand = expansion(mult = 0.04)
    ) +
    coord_cartesian(
      xlim = c(-likert_contrast_limit, likert_contrast_limit),
      clip = "on"
    ) +
    labs(
      title = unname(likert_panel_titles[question_name]),
      x = NULL,
      y = NULL
    ) +
    plot_theme(base_size = s$base) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(
        hjust = 0.5,
        face = "bold",
        size = s$title
      ),
      axis.text.x = element_text(size = s$axis_x),
      axis.text.y = element_text(
        size = if (print) s$base else s$labels * ggplot2::.pt,
        margin = margin(r = s$margin)
      ),
      axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
      axis.line.y = element_blank(),
      panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
      plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
      plot.margin = margin(6, 12, 8, 12)
    )

  if (!show_x) {
    p <- p +
      theme(
        axis.text.x = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks.x = element_blank()
      )
  }

  if (!show_labels) {
    p <- p +
      theme(axis.text.y = element_blank())
  }

  p
}
```

```{r likert-basic-contrast-figure}
#| cache: false
#| fig-width: 16
#| fig-height: 11

# Site version, or with print = TRUE the print version (audit V7).
make_likert_contrast_figure <- function(print = FALSE) {
  s <- likert_figure_sizes(print)
  contrast_p1 <- make_likert_contrast_plot(question_columns[1], show_x = FALSE, print = print)
  contrast_p2 <- make_likert_contrast_plot(
    question_columns[2], show_x = FALSE, show_labels = FALSE, print = print
  )
  contrast_p3 <- make_likert_contrast_plot(question_columns[3], show_x = TRUE, print = print)
  contrast_p4 <- make_likert_contrast_plot(
    question_columns[4], show_x = TRUE, show_labels = FALSE, print = print
  )

  # Axis caption with Basic topoplot in its accent colour, centred under the
  # data panels (the left column also holds the visualization labels).
  caption_x <- if (print) 0.556 else 0.556
  caption_size <- s$caption
  likert_contrast_caption <- ggplot() +
    annotate(
      "text",
      x = caption_x - 0.003,
      y = 0.5,
      label = "Difference in expected rating vs",
      hjust = 1,
      size = caption_size / ggplot2::.pt,
      family = "Lato",
      colour = "#222222"
    ) +
    annotate(
      "text",
      x = caption_x + 0.003,
      y = 0.5,
      label = "Basic topoplot",
      hjust = 0,
      size = caption_size / ggplot2::.pt,
      family = "Lato",
      colour = basic_accent
    ) +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, 1), clip = "off") +
    theme_void()

  ((contrast_p1 + contrast_p2) /
    (contrast_p3 + contrast_p4) /
    likert_contrast_caption) +
    plot_layout(heights = c(1, 1, if (print) 0.1 else 0.12)) &
    theme(plot.margin = if (print) margin(7, 4, 3, 4) else margin(6, 12, 6, 12))
}
```

```{r likert-contrast-summary}
#| include: false
likert_contrast_sentence <- function(question_name) {
  rows <- likert_contrasts |>
    filter(question == question_name, excludes_zero) |>
    arrange(desc(difference))
  if (nrow(rows) == 0) {
    return("no visualization differs from Basic topoplot")
  }
  paste(
    sprintf(
      "%s (%+.2f [%+.2f, %+.2f])",
      unname(likert_display_labels[as.character(rows$vistype)]),
      rows$difference, rows$lower_ci, rows$upper_ci
    ),
    collapse = "; "
  )
}

likert_sensitivity <- likert_contrasts |>
  mutate(question = as.character(question), vistype = as.character(vistype)) |>
  inner_join(likert_lmm_contrasts, by = c("question", "vistype")) |>
  mutate(
    lmm_excludes_zero = lmm_lower > 0 | lmm_upper < 0,
    agree = excludes_zero == lmm_excludes_zero
  )
```

**Contrasts against Basic topoplot** (Dunnett-adjusted 95% CIs; only intervals that exclude
zero are listed):

`r paste0("- ", question_columns, ": ", purrr::map_chr(question_columns, likert_contrast_sentence), ".", collapse = "\n")`

Differences between the uncertainty visualizations themselves were not tested, so the page
does not name a best visualization for any item.

::: {.callout-note title="Sensitivity: linear mixed model on the 1–5 ratings" collapse="true"}
```{r likert-lmm-sensitivity}
likert_sensitivity |>
  mutate(
    vistype = unname(likert_display_labels[vistype]),
    clmm = sprintf("%+.2f [%+.2f, %+.2f]", difference, lower_ci, upper_ci),
    lmm = sprintf("%+.2f [%+.2f, %+.2f]", lmm_difference, lmm_lower, lmm_upper),
    agree = if_else(agree, "yes", "**no**")
  ) |>
  select(question, vistype, clmm, lmm, agree) |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    escape = FALSE,
    col.names = c(
      "Evaluation criterion", "Visualization vs Basic",
      "Ordinal model (CLMM)", "Linear mixed model", "Same conclusion"
    ),
    caption = paste(
      "Dunnett-adjusted differences vs Basic topoplot from the ordinal model and",
      "from a linear mixed model <code>rating ~ vistype + (1 | ID)</code>"
    ),
    table.attr = kable_table_attributes
  )
```

The two models agree on whether the interval excludes zero for
`r sum(likert_sensitivity$agree)` of `r nrow(likert_sensitivity)` contrasts.
:::

```{r likert-quality-sensitivity}
#| include: false
source(project_path("scripts", "data_quality.R"))

likert_contrasts_screened <- likert_model_data |>
  filter(!as.integer(as.character(ID)) %in% flagged_ids) |>
  mutate(ID = droplevels(ID)) |>
  (\(data) split(data, data$question))() |>
  imap_dfr(function(data_question, question_name) {
    fit <- clmm(rating_ord ~ vistype + (1 | ID), data = data_question, Hess = TRUE)
    question_emmeans <- emmeans(fit, ~ vistype, mode = "mean.class")
    set.seed(20261118)  # adjust = "mvt" integrates numerically (Monte Carlo)
    contrast(
      question_emmeans,
      method = "trt.vs.ctrl",
      ref = which(question_emmeans@levels$vistype == "basic"),
      adjust = "mvt"
    ) |>
      confint() |>
      as.data.frame() |>
      transmute(
        question = question_name,
        vistype = stringr::str_remove(contrast, " - basic$"),
        screened_difference = estimate,
        screened_lower = asymp.LCL,
        screened_upper = asymp.UCL
      )
  })

likert_quality_sensitivity <- likert_contrasts |>
  mutate(question = as.character(question), vistype = as.character(vistype)) |>
  inner_join(likert_contrasts_screened, by = c("question", "vistype")) |>
  mutate(
    shift = screened_difference - difference,
    screened_excludes_zero = screened_lower > 0 | screened_upper < 0,
    agree = excludes_zero == screened_excludes_zero
  )
```

**Sensitivity: quality screen.** Without the `r length(flagged_ids)` participants flagged
for speeding or straight-lining (see the [Quality control](quality.qmd) page), the contrasts against Basic move by at
most `r sprintf("%.2f", max(abs(likert_quality_sensitivity$shift)))` scale points, and
`r sum(!likert_quality_sensitivity$agree)` of `r nrow(likert_quality_sensitivity)` intervals
change their position relative to zero.

```{r}
  arrange(question, vistype) |>
  mutate(vistype = table_vistype(vistype)) |>

model_table_note(paste0(
```

## Summary of the subjective-rating results

```{r subjective-summary-text}
#| include: false
#| cache: false
# Every number below comes from objects computed above. A visualization is
# rated higher or lower than Basic only when its Dunnett-adjusted interval
# excludes zero; otherwise the text says that the interval includes 0.
subjective_summary_item <- function(question_name) {
  estimates <- likert_estimates |>
    filter(question == question_name) |>
    mutate(vistype = as.character(vistype))
  basic <- estimates |> filter(vistype == "basic")
  others <- estimates |> filter(vistype != "basic")
  highest <- others |> slice_max(estimated_rating, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)
  lowest <- others |> slice_min(estimated_rating, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)
  contrasts <- likert_contrasts |>
    filter(question == question_name) |>
    mutate(vistype = as.character(vistype)) |>
    arrange(desc(difference))
  describe <- function(rows) {
    knitr::combine_words(sprintf(
      "%s (%s, 95%% CI %s to %s)",
      table_vistype(rows$vistype),
      signed_text(rows$difference, 2),
      signed_text(rows$lower_ci, 2),
      signed_text(rows$upper_ci, 2)
    ))
  }
  higher <- contrasts |> filter(lower_ci > 0)
  lower <- contrasts |> filter(upper_ci < 0)
  unclear <- contrasts |> filter(lower_ci <= 0, upper_ci >= 0)
  paste0(
    "**", question_name, ".** Basic topoplot ",
    sprintf("%.2f", basic$estimated_rating), " (95% CI ",
    sprintf("%.2f–%.2f", basic$lower_ci, basic$upper_ci),
    "); the uncertainty visualizations ranged from ",
    sprintf("%.2f", lowest$estimated_rating), " (", table_vistype(lowest$vistype),
    ") to ", sprintf("%.2f", highest$estimated_rating), " (",
    table_vistype(highest$vistype), "). ",
    if (nrow(higher) > 0) paste0("Rated higher than Basic: ", describe(higher), ". ") else "",
    if (nrow(lower) > 0) paste0("Rated lower than Basic: ", describe(lower), ". ") else "",
    if (nrow(unclear) == nrow(contrasts)) {
      "No visualization differed clearly from Basic: all six intervals included 0."
    } else if (nrow(unclear) > 0) {
      paste0(
        "The interval", if (nrow(unclear) > 1) "s" else "", " for ",
        knitr::combine_words(table_vistype(unclear$vistype)), " included 0."
      )
    } else {
      ""
    }
  )
}

subjective_po_rejected <- sum(po_tests$p_value < .05)
subjective_n_contrasts <- nrow(likert_contrasts)
subjective_n_clear <- sum(likert_contrasts$excludes_zero)
subjective_n_higher <- sum(likert_contrasts$lower_ci > 0)
subjective_n_lower <- sum(likert_contrasts$upper_ci < 0)
```

- **Expected ratings and contrasts with Basic topoplot** (expected rating on the 1–5 scale
  for a typical participant from the ordinal model; differences are Dunnett-adjusted for
  the six comparisons with Basic within each item).
`r paste0("  - ", purrr::map_chr(question_columns, subjective_summary_item), collapse = "\n")`
- **Overall.** `r subjective_n_clear` of `r subjective_n_contrasts` contrasts excluded 0:
  `r subjective_n_higher` with a higher and `r subjective_n_lower` with a lower rating than
  Basic topoplot. Differences between the uncertainty visualizations themselves were not
  tested.
- **Proportional-odds check.** The likelihood-ratio test rejected proportional odds for
  `r subjective_po_rejected` of `r nrow(po_tests)` items (*p* from
  `r format_p_value(min(po_tests$p_value))` to `r format_p_value(max(po_tests$p_value))`).
  The page therefore reports expected ratings rather than odds ratios; they differ from
  the raw means by at most `r sprintf("%.2f", max_raw_model_difference)` scale points.
- **Sensitivity: quality screen.** Without the `r length(flagged_ids)` flagged
  participants, the contrasts moved by at most
  `r sprintf("%.2f", max(abs(likert_quality_sensitivity$shift)))` scale points, and
  `r sum(!likert_quality_sensitivity$agree)` of `r nrow(likert_quality_sensitivity)`
  intervals changed their position relative to 0.
- **Sensitivity: linear mixed model.** A linear mixed model on the 1–5 ratings, which
  does not assume proportional odds, reached the same conclusion (interval excluding 0
  or not) for `r sum(likert_sensitivity$agree)` of `r nrow(likert_sensitivity)`
  contrasts.
- **Caveat.** The visualizations were listed in the same order for every participant
  (Basic topoplot last), so order effects cannot be separated from differences between
  visualizations.
